text:
Define the following along with appropriate examples:
(a) Type casting
(b) Literals
modelAnswer:
(a) Type casting is the explicit conversion of a value of one data type into another using the cast operator, e.g. int n = (int) 23.8; converts the double 23.8 into the int 23.
(b) Literals are explicit, fixed data values written directly in a program, e.g. 25 (integer literal), 3.14 (floating literal), 'A' (character literal), "Hi" (string literal).
keyPoints: Type casting uses the (type) operator to force a conversion, e.g. (int), (double)
Narrowing casts (double to int) can lose precision/data
Literals are the literal, unchanging values typed directly into code
Every literal has an associated data type (int, double, char, String, boolean)

chapter: Elementary Concepts of Objects and Classes
text:
Define the following along with appropriate examples:
(a) Object
(b) Encapsulation
modelAnswer:
(a) An object is an instance of a class; it is a real-world entity having state (attributes/fields) and behaviour (methods). Example: if 'Car' is a class, then myCar = new Car(); creates an object named myCar.
(b) Encapsulation is the OOP principle of binding data (fields) and the methods that act on that data together within a single class, and restricting direct access to the data from outside the class. Example: declaring fields as 'private' and providing public getter/setter methods to access them.
keyPoints: An object is created from a class using the 'new' keyword
A class can have many objects, each with its own copy of the instance data
Encapsulation hides the internal data of a class from outside interference
Private fields + public methods is the common way encapsulation is implemented

text: Define 'Empty loop' with an appropriate example.
modelAnswer:
An empty loop is a loop that does not contain any statement inside its body; it is typically used to deliberately waste a fixed number of CPU cycles (a 'time delay' loop). Example:
for(int i=0; i<10000; i++);
keyPoints: The loop body is empty — only the semicolon ends the loop statement
Commonly used to create a time delay
The loop variable still increments every iteration even though nothing else happens

text: In procedural programming, more emphasis is given to procedures/functions rather than data, while object-oriented programming emphasises data. Explain this difference with an example.
modelAnswer: In procedural programming (e.g. C), a program is organised as a series of functions/procedures that act upon data passed to them, so the design focuses on 'what steps to perform'. In object-oriented programming (e.g. Java), the program is organised around objects that bundle data and the methods that operate on that data together, so the design focuses on 'which objects exist and what they can do'. For example, to print a student's details procedurally, a function printStudent(name, marks) is written; in OOP, a Student class is defined with its own fields and a display() method, and this method is called on a Student object.
keyPoints: Procedural: emphasis on functions/procedures acting on data
Object-oriented: emphasis on objects that combine data and behaviour
OOP improves reusability and data security via encapsulation

text: Define tokens in Java. Name any two types of tokens and explain Boolean literals.
modelAnswer: A token is the smallest individual unit of a Java program that the compiler recognises, such as a keyword, identifier, literal, operator or punctuator. Two types of tokens are Keywords (e.g. int, if, class) and Literals (e.g. 25, 'A', "Hi"). Boolean literals are the two reserved values true and false, which represent the only two possible values of the boolean data type.
keyPoints: Tokens: keywords, identifiers, literals, operators, punctuators/separators
Keywords have special, predefined meaning and cannot be used as identifiers
Boolean literals are exactly 'true' and 'false' (lowercase, no quotes)

text: Write the range and size of the int data type.
modelAnswer: The int data type in Java occupies 4 bytes (32 bits) of memory, and its range is -2^31 to 2^31-1, i.e. -2147483648 to 2147483647.
keyPoints: Size: 4 bytes (32 bits)
int is the default type for integer literals without a suffix

text: Differentiate between println() and print() statements in Java.
modelAnswer: print() displays the given output on the screen and leaves the cursor on the same line, so the next output continues on the same line. println() displays the output and then moves the cursor to the beginning of the next line, so subsequent output starts on a new line.
keyPoints: print(): no line break after output
println(): moves to a new line after output
Both belong to the System.out object

text: Differentiate between a variable and a constant in Java.
modelAnswer: A variable is a named memory location whose value can change during the execution of a program (e.g. int marks = 50; marks = 60;). A constant is a named memory location whose value is fixed and cannot be changed once initialised — it is declared using the 'final' keyword (e.g. final double PI = 3.14;).
keyPoints: Variable: value can be reassigned during program execution
Constant: declared with 'final', value cannot change after initialisation
Attempting to reassign a final variable causes a compile-time error

text:
Read the given passage and answer the following questions:
Packages are Java's way of grouping a number of related classes and/or interfaces together into a single unit. Packages make programs more organised and compact, and they save effort because classes' code can be reused.
(a) Which keyword is used for including a package in our program?
(b) Which is a default package in Java?
modelAnswer:
(a) The 'import' keyword is used to include a package in a program, e.g. import java.util.Scanner;
(b) java.lang is the default package in Java — it is automatically imported into every Java program without an explicit import statement.
keyPoints: import keyword brings a package's classes into scope
java.lang is implicitly available in every program (contains System, Math, String, etc.)

text: Differentiate between a Run Time Error and a Compile Time (Syntax) Error.
modelAnswer: A Compile Time (Syntax) Error occurs when the code violates the grammar/rules of Java and is detected by the compiler before the program runs (e.g. a missing semicolon or misspelled keyword), preventing the program from compiling at all. A Run Time Error occurs while the program is executing, after it has compiled successfully, usually due to an illegal operation such as division by zero or an invalid array index, and it causes the program to terminate abnormally (throwing an exception).
keyPoints: Syntax error: caught by the compiler, before execution, program doesn't compile
Runtime error: occurs during execution of an already-compiled program
Example runtime error: ArithmeticException from division by zero
The initialisation (i=0) is moved before the loop
The loop body is placed inside the do block
The update (i++) is placed at the end of the do block
The for loop's test condition becomes the while condition

text: Explain unary and binary operators in Java with an example of each.
modelAnswer: A unary operator acts on only one operand, e.g. the increment operator in x++ (operand: x) or the unary minus in -y. A binary operator acts on two operands, e.g. the addition operator in a+b or the relational operator in a>b.
keyPoints: Unary: one operand, e.g. ++, --, unary +, unary -, !
Binary: two operands, e.g. +, -, *, /, %, >, &&

text:
Define the following:
(a) Fall through
(b) Selection Construct
modelAnswer:
(a) Fall-through is the behaviour in a switch statement where, in the absence of a break statement at the end of a matching case, control continues ('falls through') into the statements of the following case(s) as well.
(b) A selection construct is a programming construct (such as if-else or switch) that chooses one among several possible paths of execution, based on the result of a test condition.
keyPoints: Fall-through happens only when a case block is missing 'break'
Selection constructs: if, if-else, if-else-if, switch
A selection construct always evaluates a condition to decide which branch runs

text: What are escape sequences in Java? Give an example.
modelAnswer: Escape sequences are special character combinations, starting with a backslash (\), used to represent non-graphic (non-printable) characters that cannot be typed directly from the keyboard, such as a newline or tab. Example: '\n' represents a newline character and '\t' represents a horizontal tab.
keyPoints: Escape sequences begin with a backslash (\)
Common examples: \n (newline), \t (tab), \\ (backslash), \' (single quote)

text: Differentiate between literals and keywords in Java. Give appropriate examples to support your answer.
modelAnswer: A literal is an explicit, fixed data value written directly in the source code, e.g. 25, 3.14, 'A', "Hi", true. A keyword is a reserved word that carries a special, predefined meaning to the Java compiler and can never be used as an identifier, e.g. int, if, class, final, static.
keyPoints: Literals represent actual data values of a particular type
Keywords are reserved words that control the structure/meaning of the program
A keyword can never be used as a variable name; a literal is not a name at all

text: Mention two differences between the = operator and the == operator in Java.
modelAnswer: The '=' operator is the assignment operator; it assigns the value on its right-hand side to the variable on its left (e.g. x = 5;). The '==' operator is the equality (relational) operator; it compares two values and returns a boolean result (true/false) indicating whether they are equal (e.g. x == 5).
keyPoints: '=' assigns a value; '==' compares two values
'=' expression has no boolean result; '==' always evaluates to true or false
Using '=' where '==' is intended is a common source of logical errors

text:
Arrange the following primitive data types in ascending order of size: char, double, int, byte.
Also mention the range of the data type that is smallest in size.
modelAnswer:
Ascending order of size: byte (1 byte) < char (2 bytes) < int (4 bytes) < double (8 bytes).
The smallest data type, byte, has the range -128 to 127.
keyPoints: byte=1 byte, char=2 bytes, int=4 bytes, double=8 bytes
byte is the smallest primitive numeric type, range -128 to 127

S = 1+2 + (1+2+3) + (1+2+3+4) + ... up to n terms, each term divided respectively by 1x2, 1x2x3, 1x2x3x4, ...
keyPoints: Each term's numerator is the sum 1+2+...+i for an increasing i
Each term's denominator is the factorial i! for the same i
The overall sum accumulates n such term values

text: Write a Java program to input a number from the user and check whether it is prime or not. If the number is prime, find the reverse of that number. If the input number is composite, print all the factors of that number.
keyPoints: If prime, reverse the digits of the number
If composite, print every factor of the number from 1 to the number itself

text:
Write a Java program to input a number and check whether it is a Harshad Number or not. [A Harshad Number is an integer that is divisible by the sum of its digits.]
Sample Input: 200 -> sum of digits = 2, 200 is divisible by 2 -> Harshad Number
Sample Input: 273 -> sum of digits = 12, 273 is not divisible by 12 -> not a Harshad Number
keyPoints: Sum the digits of the number using %10 and /10
A number is Harshad if it divides evenly by its own digit sum

text:
A cloth showroom has announced festival discounts and gifts based on the total cost of items purchased:
Total Cost              Discount    Gift
Up to Rs. 2,000            5%      Calculator
Rs. 2,001 to Rs. 5,000    10%      School Bag
Rs. 5,001 to Rs. 10,000   15%      Wall Clock
Above Rs. 10,000          20%      Wrist Watch
Write a program to input the total cost, then compute and display the amount to be paid along with the gift.
keyPoints: Each cost slab has its own discount rate AND its own gift
Amount to pay = total cost - (total cost * discount rate)

text:

(i) S = -1-3-5-7-...-20 (odd negative numbers from -1 down to the one nearest -20)
(ii) Print and find the sum of all the multiples of 5 that lie between 0 and 100
keyPoints: Series (i) runs through odd numbers 1,3,5,...,19, each made negative
Series (ii) runs through multiples of 5 from 5 to 100

text:
Write a menu driven program to print the first 10 terms of the following series:
(1) 0, 7, 26, 63, 124, ...

text:
Write the Java program to print the following pattern using nested loops, alternating 'a' and 'b' row by row (each row repeating its own letter a number of times equal to the row number):
a
bb
aaa
bbbb
aaaaa
keyPoints: Odd rows print 'a', even rows print 'b'

text:
Convert the following mathematical expression to an equivalent Java statement:
s = (c*d)^6 + √((c + d*5) / 7)
modelAnswer: s = Math.pow(c*d, 6) + Math.sqrt((c + d*5) / 7);
keyPoints: Use Math.pow(c*d, 6) for the sixth power
Use Math.sqrt() for the square root
Keep (c + d*5)/7 inside the brackets of Math.sqrt

text:
In order to sell an old car, the depreciated value can be calculated as per the tariff given below:
No. of months used     Rate of Depreciation
1-12 months            12%
13-24 months           15%
25-48 months           18%
Above 48 months        25%
Write a program in Java to input the showroom price and the number of months the car is used. Calculate the depreciated value. Display the original price of the car, the depreciated value and the final amount to be paid.
keyPoints: Accept price (double) and months (int) using Scanner
Use an if-else-if ladder to choose the depreciation rate by months
Depreciation = price * rate / 100; final amount = price - depreciation
Display original price, depreciation and final amount

text:
Write a menu driven program in Java to do the following:
1. Input a number n from the user. Check and display whether the number is a Special number or not.
[A Special number is a positive integer which has more than two factors. E.g. 4 is a Special number as it has 1, 2 and 4 as factors; 15 is a Special number as it has 1, 3, 5, 15 as factors; 3 is not a Special number as it has only 1 and 3 as its factors.]
2. Compute and display the sum of the following series:
S = 1 + 3 + 6 + 10 + 15 + ... up to x terms, where x is entered by the user.
keyPoints: Use switch on the user's choice with a default for invalid input
Count factors with n % i == 0; Special if the count is more than 2
Each series term is the previous term plus i (triangular numbers)
Accumulate the terms in a sum variable and display it

text:
Write a Java program to generate the following pattern using nested loops:
1
3 5
5 7 9
7 9 11 13
9 11 13 15 17
keyPoints: Outer loop runs for 5 rows
Row i starts with the odd number 2*i - 1
Inner loop prints i numbers, each 2 more than the previous
println() after each row moves to the next line

chapter: Elementary Concepts of Objects and Classes
text: Write any two advantages of Object Oriented Programming (OOP).
modelAnswer:
1. Reusability: through inheritance, existing classes can be reused to create new classes, saving time and effort.
2. Data security: through encapsulation and data hiding, data is bound with the methods that use it and is protected from accidental misuse.
(Other valid points: easier maintenance and modification of code, modelling of real-world objects, polymorphism allows flexible code.)
keyPoints: Reusability of code through inheritance
Data hiding/security through encapsulation
Easier maintenance and modelling of real-world entities

chapter: Elementary Concepts of Objects and Classes
text:
Define the following:
(a) Syntax error
(b) Abstraction
modelAnswer:
(a) A syntax error is an error caused by violating the grammatical rules of the programming language (e.g. a missing semicolon or misspelt keyword). It is detected by the compiler at compile time.
(b) Abstraction is the OOP principle of representing only the essential features of an object while hiding the background details and internal implementation.
keyPoints: Syntax error: violation of the language's grammar rules
Syntax errors are caught by the compiler at compile time
Abstraction: showing essential features and hiding background details
Initialise i = 1 before the do block
Keep the if (i % 10 == 0) check inside the body
Increment i inside the body and test i <= 100 in the while condition

text:
Rewrite the following program segment using an if-else construct in Java:
String s = (x > y) ? "x is greater" : (x < y) ? "y is greater" : "x and y are equal";
keyPoints: First condition x > y assigns "x is greater"
The nested ternary becomes else if (x < y)
The final else assigns "x and y are equal"

text:
Write a menu driven program in Java to calculate and display the sum of the following:
(i) R = 4 - 8 + 16 - 32 + 64 ... up to n terms [where n is entered by the user]
(ii) S = 0.5 + 0.25 + 0.125 + ... up to 6 terms
keyPoints: The i-th term of R is 2^(i+1): add for odd i, subtract for even i
The i-th term of S is 1/2^i, i.e. 0.5, 0.25, 0.125 ...

switch-case menu with a default for an invalid choice

text:
A car-rental company charges rent on cars on the following basis:
No. of days            Rent
First 5 days           Rs. 2000 per day
Next 5 days            Rs. 1000 per day
Next 3 days            Rs. 800 per day
More than 13 days      Rs. 500 per day
Write a Java program that accepts the car number, customer name and number of days the car is rented. Calculate the charge to be paid by the customer based on the above criteria. The output must be printed in the format:
Car No.    Customer Name    No. of days    Charge

text:
Write a Java program to accept 2 positive integers m and n. Check and display all the palindrome numbers between the two integers m and n. Also display the frequency of palindrome numbers.
Sample Input:
Enter first positive integer (m): 11
Enter second positive integer (n): 19
Sample Output:
Palindromes between the given range are : 11
Frequency is : 1
keyPoints: Loop i from m to n
Reverse each number using % 10 and / 10 on a copy
A number is a palindrome if its reverse equals the number

text:
Write a Java program to accept a number from the user. Check and display if the number is an Abundant number or not.
[An abundant number is a positive integer where the sum of its proper divisors (divisors excluding the number itself) is greater than the number itself.]
Sample input: 12
Sample output: 12 is an Abundant number
(Proper divisors are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6; their sum = 16; since 16 > 12, 12 is an abundant number.)
keyPoints: Loop i from 1 to n-1 (proper divisors exclude n)
Add i to sum when n % i == 0
Abundant if sum of proper divisors > n

text:
Write the Java expression for the following:
(mn + |m|) / (m + n)
modelAnswer: (m*n + Math.abs(m)) / (m + n)
keyPoints: mn must be written as m*n
|m| is written as Math.abs(m)

text:
A laptop company gives a discount to its customers based on the number of laptops purchased. If the number of laptops is more than three, the customers get a discount of 10% on the total cost, otherwise the discount is zero.
Define a class "laptop" to accept the name of the company [String], name of the customer [String], number of laptops [int], and the price of each laptop [double] from the user using Scanner class methods only.
Calculate the discount [double] and the amount to be paid [double] by the customer.
Discount = number of laptops × price × 10%
Amount to be paid = number of laptops × price - discount
Print all the details.
keyPoints: Use nextLine() for Strings, nextInt() and nextDouble() for numbers
Discount is 10% of n × price only when n > 3, else 0
Amount = n × price - discount
Print all input details along with discount and amount

text: What are relational operators in Java? Name any two relational operators.
modelAnswer: Relational operators are used to compare two values; the result of the comparison is a boolean value (true or false). Examples: > (greater than), < (less than), >= (greater than or equal to), <= (less than or equal to), == (equal to), != (not equal to).
keyPoints: Relational operators compare two values
The result is boolean: true or false

text:
Write a menu-driven program to calculate the area of an equilateral triangle and a scalene triangle as per the user's choice (using switch case only).
(i) Scalene triangle area = √(s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)), where a, b, c are the sides and s = (a + b + c) / 2
(ii) Equilateral triangle area = (√3 / 4) × a², where a = side of the triangle
keyPoints: Display a menu and read the choice
Case 1: s = (a+b+c)/2, area = Math.sqrt(s*(s-a)*(s-b)*(s-c))
Case 2: area = Math.sqrt(3)/4 * a * a
break after each case and a default for an invalid choice
